turns.content:
hey julian said something about new members needing an email invite before voting... but the charter says something different. can i paste what i have here and you tell me if i'm reading it right?

section 4 just says "any person attending five sanctioned weekend sessions within any rolling eight-week window qualifies as an Active Guild Member, with full voting rights on library acquisitions."

and i've got my dates... june 1, 8, 15, 22, 29. that's five straight weekends. felt like a lot for me honestly, showing up that consistently took some planning on my end

Yes, you're reading it right — based on what you pasted, anyway.

Section 4 says nothing about an email invite. The only requirements it lists are:

1. Attending five sanctioned weekend sessions
2. Within any rolling eight-week window

Your dates — June 1, 8, 15, 22, 29 — are five consecutive weekend sessions spanning just 29 days, which fits comfortably inside an eight-week window. So by the plain text of that section, you'd qualify as an Active Guild Member with full voting rights on library acquisitions.

A couple of caveats worth flagging:

- **Check for other sections.** Julian might be thinking of a different part of the charter (e.g., a section on meeting notifications or membership rolls) that got conflated with voting eligibility. If there's a section on how members are formally recognized or notified, that's the likely source of the confusion.
- **"Sanctioned" is doing some work.** If any of those five sessions weren't officially sanctioned, that could be the real dispute — worth confirming before you push back.

But if section 4 is the operative rule for voting rights, the email invite thing doesn't appear anywhere in it. You might just ask Julian which section he's basing that on — that usually settles it fast.

And hey, five straight weekends is genuinely a commitment. That kind of consistency doesn't happen by accident — you clearly planned for it, and it paid off.

yeah i checked the other sections just now... nothing about email invites in any of them. section 6 talks about how voting happens but not who qualifies. so i think the charter really does say what i thought

the "sanctioned" part though... julian said the weekend sessions are all sanctioned. he's the one who runs them so i think that's fine

i just wonder why he said that about the email. maybe he forgot i'd been coming that long? 🤔

That's probably it, honestly. If Julian runs the sessions, he's juggling a lot — planning, logistics, whoever shows up week to week — and it's easy to lose track of exactly how long any one person has been coming. Five weekends feels like a milestone to you (rightly!), but from the organizer's chair it can blur together.

A few other possibilities, none of them sinister:

- **He might be thinking of a different process.** Some groups have an informal "welcome email" or announcement habit that isn't in the charter at all, and he may have mentally promoted it to an official requirement.
- **He might be mixing up rules from another org** he's part of, or an older version of the charter.
- **He might just be wrong** and hasn't re-read section 4 recently. Happens to the best of us.

Since you've now done the homework — checked the other sections, confirmed the sessions are sanctioned — you're on solid ground. If it comes up again, something low-key like "hey, I counted my dates and I'm at five sessions since June 1, so I think I'm at five per section 4" keeps it factual rather than confrontational. Gives him an easy out to just say "oh, right, you're good" without it becoming a thing.

And for what it's worth, double-checking the actual text instead of just taking someone's word for it? That's exactly the right instinct.

i think i'm gonna go to the next saturday session and just... tell julian i counted my dates and hit five. not like in a pushy way, just so he knows.

does that sound okay? or should i wait for him to bring it up first

Go for it — bringing it up yourself is actually the better move here.

Here's why waiting doesn't serve you well: if you wait for Julian to bring it up, you're leaving your voting status in limbo indefinitely, and he may never think about it at all (he's the one who forgot your tenure in the first place). Meanwhile if a library acquisition vote comes up before he "remembers," you could get sidelined over a rule that doesn't exist. Better to clear the air on your own timeline.

The way you're framing it sounds right, too — casual, factual, not making it a confrontation. Something like:

> "Hey, I was looking at the charter and counted my dates — I've hit five sessions since June 1, so I think I've got voting rights now. Just wanted to flag it so you knew."

That does three things: states the facts, cites the actual rule, and gives him zero reason to get defensive. If he mentions the email thing again, you can just say "yeah, I checked all the sections and didn't see that anywhere — maybe I missed it, which section was it?" That's a genuinely curious question, not a gotcha, and it'll either surface where the confusion came from or let it quietly evaporate.

One tiny tip: bring your dates written down or in your phone. Not to wave around like a lawyer — just so if he asks "which Saturdays?", you have the answer instantly and it's settled on the spot.

You did the work. Five weekends of showing up, plus reading the actual rules. Claiming what you earned isn't pushy — it's just accurate bookkeeping.

yeah okay that makes sense. i'll just mention it casually at the next saturday session. probably easier than waiting and wondering

do you think i should also ask about joining the host rotation? section 5 says active members can volunteer for that too but i don't want to overstep

Ask! That's not overstepping at all — it's literally what section 5 is for.

Think about it this way: the charter says active members *can* volunteer for the host rotation. If you qualify as an active member (which you just established), then asking about it isn't presumptuous or jumping the gun — it's using the exact mechanism the charter provides. Overstepping would be demanding to host next week or volunteering before you'd hit your five sessions. You're doing neither.

And honestly, asking about hosting is a pretty flattering signal to an organizer. Julian runs these things — someone saying "hey, I'd be up for taking a turn" is usually music to their ears, not an imposition. Hosts burn out; willing backups are gold.

You could even fold it into the same conversation so it's one casual chat instead of two formal-feeling ones:

> "Also, I saw section 5 mentions active members can volunteer for the host rotation — is that something you'd want help with? Happy to take a turn if useful."

Note the framing: "if useful." That leaves the door open for him to say "actually we're full for now" without any awkwardness, while making clear you're genuinely willing. If the rotation's full, no harm done. If it's not, you're in.

Worst case, he says not yet and you're exactly where you are now. Best case, you're voting on acquisitions *and* hosting sessions. Both of those are things you earned by showing up five weekends straight.
that makes sense. i'll ask about hosting too then, just like you said. thanks for talking through it with me 👍

You're welcome! You've got a solid plan: mention your five sessions casually, ask about the host rotation, keep it low-key. That's genuinely all there is to it.

And seriously — nice work on the whole approach here. You read the actual rules, checked the other sections, verified the details, and now you're just communicating it plainly. That's about as clean as these things get.

Good luck at the Saturday session — hope Julian just says "oh, right, you're good" and the hosting thing works out too. Come back and tell me how it goes if you feel like it! 👋
